Acrobatic Cheerleader: Solid early filler for GW Survival. A vanilla 2/2 that becomes a 2/2 flyer if it survives a swing, so the 53.5% GIH is doing honest 2-drop work — you play it as curve-filler and survival glue, not a card you prioritize. Fine, replaceable.
Cult Healer: Filler body. The 53.1% GIH and negative IWD say a vanilla 3/3 that occasionally lifelinks — it needs a real Eerie density (WU/UB) to matter and even then it's a curve-filler, not a payoff. Late playable in enchantment decks, cuttable elsewhere.
Dazzling Theater // Prop Room: Trap. A 39.8% GIH with a −8.8 IWD and an F grade is about as damning as the data gets — convoke on creature spells and a vigilance-lite untap effect do nothing to stabilize a board, and you pay four-plus mana to find out. The 18% play rate is people learning their lesson. Don't run it.
Dollmaker's Shop // Porcelain Gallery: First-pickable Room bomb — 62.8% GIH on a 90% play rate and 1.4 ALSA is the real deal, not a synergy mirage. The cheap front half snowballs a wide board of Toys, then Porcelain Gallery flips every creature into a lethal team all at once. Goes in any go-wide white deck (RW, GW, WU) and wins games unassisted.
Emerge from the Cocoon: Playable reanimation glue for BW, not a slam. The 54.3% GIH is honest role-player output — five mana, sorcery-speed, and it only shines when your yard holds a fatty, which the Orzhov reanimator deck engineers. In a fair pile it's an overcosted lifegain spell; grab it once you're committed, not P1.
Enduring Innocence: First-pick white bomb and the RW/WU token engine's ceiling: lifelink plus recurring card draw off your 2-power tokens, and it comes back as an enchantment when killed so it demands exile answers. 60% GIH with a 1.6 ALSA and 90% play is a real slam, not a synergy mirage — the enter trigger only needs one small creature per turn.
Ethereal Armor: Role-player, and only in a dedicated build. The 57.5% GIH is deceptive Aura math from stacked WU/GW enchantment decks where +1/+1-per-enchantment plus first strike snowballs; the C grade is the honest floor. The one-for-one blowout risk means it's a payoff you play when Eerie is already your deck, not a P2 pick.
Exorcise: Solid removal, take it early. It exiles rather than feeding the yard, which matters in this Delirium/reanimator format, and the power-4-or-greater clause is rarely a problem since the format's real threats are big. The 56.6% GIH and 88% play rate confirm it's a reliable maindeck answer, just not premium the way Sheltered by Ghosts is; grade it a notch above the B-.
Fear of Abduction: Strong early white uncommon and Ben's #1 — a 5/5 flyer that Vindicates a threat on entry. The C grade badly underrates it; trust the 3.3 ALSA and drafters' feet. Two catches keep the WR merely-good rather than bomb-tier: you must exile your own creature to cast, and the removal is only temporary (both come back if it dies). Best in WU tempo/eerie.
Fear of Immobility: Solid tempo filler. A 4/4 that taps-and-stuns on entry is a legitimate common — the body dodges Nowhere to Run (−3/−3) and the stun buys a turn against their best attacker or unblocks yours. The flat 55% is honest maindeck value; it also counts as an enchantment for WU/UB eerie.
Fear of Surveillance: Solid early playable, not a priority. A 2/2 vigilance two-drop that surveils on attack is fine curve-filler that quietly fuels delirium/graveyard decks, but the 55.5% GIH and near-zero IWD say it's a body you're happy to have, not one that swings games. Take it mid-pack; the 90% play rate is floor, not ceiling.
Friendly Ghost: Solid mid-pick playable. A 2/4 flyer for 4 already blocks the format's ground clog and clears the four-toughness removal bar, and the +2/+4 ETB is a real combat blowout or a way to punch through. The 55.6% GIH reflects a clean, no-synergy filler flyer — take it, don't reach.
Ghostly Dancers: Bomb — near-P1P1. A 2/5 flyer that walls the ground while its eerie trigger spits out 3/1 flyers off every enchantment or Room unlock, and it rebuys an enchantment on entry. The 64.5% GIH and 1.5 ALSA are real; it's an A- engine that also fits any WU/UB eerie shell as a raw stabilizer-plus-threat.
Glimmer Seeker: Solid role-player and an easy include in any white deck. The 57% GIH with +2.1 IWD is honest: a 3/3 that either draws or builds a Glimmer engine once tapped, so it fuels Eerie/Survival synergy. Ben's alternate #3 white uncommon — take it around pick 4-5, not over premium removal.
Grand Entryway // Elegant Rotunda: Solid WU/enchantment common — 54.5% GIH at an 84% play rate is real, even if the flat IWD says it's a synergy piece, not a bomb. You get a Glimmer body plus a two-target pump across two unlocks, and critically it's a cheap enchantment that stacks eerie triggers. First playable, higher in Azorius Eerie.
Hardened Escort: Solid GW-only role-player, not a maindeck default elsewhere. The 2/4 body is a fine blocker, but the 53.8% GIH and slightly negative IWD say the attack trigger only matters when it's clearing a path for Survival attackers, as LoL flags. Fine filler in Selesnya, close to sideboard anywhere else.
Jump Scare: Filler combat trick that overperforms its role — the 55.3% GIH is buoyed by a near-flat IWD (-0.2), meaning it wins games it's already winning rather than swinging them. One-mana +2/+2 with flying is a fine surprise blowout for aggressive white, but it's replaceable; last-playable, not a priority.
Leyline of Hope: Trap/sideboard filler. Free turn-zero drop is cute but it does nothing until you're already 7 life ahead, which in a grindy graveyard format is a win-more condition. F grade and 1.3% play with null WR confirm the read; leave it in the pack.
Lionheart Glimmer: Solid playable and a genuine WU/GW Eerie enabler — a 2/5 Ward 2 body that anytime it attacks pumps your team, hard to remove under the 4-toughness benchmark. The 55.6% GIH and 83% play rate are earned from board-centric enchantment decks; a fine early pick that also feeds Eerie triggers as a permanent.
Living Phone: Filler; last-pickable body. A 2/1 for 3 whose death dig only fetches small creatures, and the negative IWD (-3.2) plus 20% play rate confirm it drags your deck down when drawn. Playable in a token/aristocrats or go-wide shell that wants a cheap sacrifice fodder body, but never a card you're happy maindecking.
Optimistic Scavenger: Premium WU eerie enabler and a near-slam one-drop — 60.7% GIH with a 64.7% OH WR and +6.0 IWD means it's pulling weight from turn one, not just late. Every enchantment/room drops a counter anywhere you want, so it snowballs a board or protects your best attacker. Take it high in any white enchantment seat.
Orphans of the Wheat: GW Survival role-player, not a bomb. Tapping your team pumps it huge but leaves you defenseless and turns off blocks — the −1.5 IWD and early ALSA (4.4) say it wants a wide aggressive board and underperforms as a topdeck. Fine two-drop for the Survival deck, replaceable elsewhere.
Overlord of the Mistmoors: First-pick bomb, take over almost anything. Impending 4 for {2}{W}{W} drops two 2/1 flyers on turn four and repeats on every attack once it becomes a 6/6 — that's board dominance across the curve. 68% GIH with +15.9 IWD and 1.2 ALSA is elite; A grade undersells how flexible the cast is.
Patched Plaything: Aggressive role-player, not the bomb the 80% play rate implies. Cast from hand it's a 2/1 double striker for 3 — fine early beats — but the negative IWD says it stops mattering as games go long. Best in RW/aggro; the counters melt if manifested/reanimated. Solid, replaceable body.
Possessed Goat: Filler mana sink, borderline maindeck. A W 1/1 that eventually becomes a 4/4 demon for {3}+discard, but the 25% play rate and D+ tell the story — it does nothing early and the payoff is slow. Only in aggressive white decks short on bodies, and even then it's replaceable.
Reluctant Role Model: Strong early creature and a snowball threat for GW Survival. The 1.9 ALSA and B grade track the +2.2 IWD — a two-drop that grows every turn and, critically, dumps its counters onto a fresh body when anything dies, so it never feels wasted. Trades up all game; take it P1-P2 range.
Savior of the Small: Below-rate role-player. The 3/4 body dodges Dragonfire, but the D+ grade and sub-51% GIH expose the recursion as slow: survival needs it tapped, and returning only MV-3-or-less creatures is a modest grind. Fine filler in GW Survival where the counters and staying power matter; a late pick elsewhere.
Seized from Slumber: Premium white removal in practice — a two-mana unconditional kill on any tapped (attacking) creature, five mana if you're forced to fire it dry. The 56.2% GIH under a modest C+ grade undersells it; in a slower format you almost always find a tapped target. Take it high and play it in every white deck.
Shardmage's Rescue: Solid white protection with a premium 3.4 ALSA and 85% play rate telling the real story: it's a one-mana flash counterspell-for-removal that saves your best creature and pushes damage. The 56.4% GIH understates its tempo value. Grab it as an efficient defensive playable in any white deck; great in WU tempo.
Sheltered by Ghosts: Premier premium removal — exile any nonland permanent for 1W while buffing your creature with lifelink and ward 2. GIH WR underrates exile removal generally, yet this still posts 61.6% with +7.9 IWD because it two-for-ones. Ben calls it a top-10 uncommon and Ethan conceded he couldn't push it down; take it over almost anything. Aura fragility is the only knock.
Shepherding Spirits: Filler with a flex mode. A 4/5 flyer for six is fine but slow in a format that punishes durdly late flyers, and Plainscycling {2} is the real value — pitch it early for a land when flooded/screwed. Negative IWD and 42% play rate confirm it's a late-table body, not a pick you prioritize.
Split Up: Premium white board wipe, a P1P1-caliber rare — take it over almost anything. Choosing tapped vs. untapped lets you blow out an attack or a defensive stall while keeping your own board, and the +4.7 IWD with 2.1 ALSA and A- grade all agree. In a format that plays slower than it looks, a flexible one-sided-ish sweeper is exactly what the control decks want.
Splitskin Doll: Solid, unglamorous white two-drop that loots on entry and keeps both cards if you already have a small creature down — trivial in a go-wide/tokens white deck. The artifact type quietly helps delirium and it flickers well with Surgical Suite/Norin. 59% GIH is a real playable, not a build-around; happy maindeck filler-plus.
Surgical Suite // Hospital Room: Strong flexible enchantment — take it in any white deck. The +3.1 IWD and 88% play rate reflect two live modes: recur a 3-drop from the yard (great in WB reanimator/eerie) or a repeatable +1/+1 counter engine. Doubles as an eerie/room trigger; the B- undersells a card that's never dead.
Toby, Beastie Befriender: Strong early pick, premium in any tokens/go-wide build. Turn three you get a 1/1 plus a 4/4, and hitting four tokens hands your whole team flying — a real win condition in RW/WU. 61.6% GIH, 1.8 ALSA and +7.6 IWD confirm it plays above a random three-drop; the B+ is right.
Trapped in the Screen: Premium white removal — grab it early. Warded exile of any artifact/creature/enchantment is unconditional answer to bombs, and crucially it exiles rather than feeding delirium/reanimator yards. The +3.1 IWD and 91% play rate confirm it's a first-few-picks staple, meaningfully better than a plain O-Ring per LoL.
Unidentified Hovership: Premium — take it high. A 1WW flyer that exiles any creature with toughness 5 or less on entry (temporary, but you get a manifest dread trade-back when it dies), so it's evasion plus soft removal on one card. 61.1% GIH understates it slightly since the exile pushes past the format's removal benchmarks; crew 1 is trivial. B grade is low — trust the live number.
Unsettling Twins: Top-tier white common — take it high. It's two bodies plus a graveyard-type and Manifest Dread fuel on one card, exactly the "bread and butter" both LoL hosts wanted; the 56.9% GIH and 70% play show it's good in any white deck, not just synergy piles. Best in UW/BW where the yard and Eerie tokens compound.
Unwanted Remake: Near-trap. One-mana destroy reads premium until you notice you're handing the opponent a 2/2 AND feeding their graveyard — actively bad in a Delirium/Reanimator format where you want exile, not gift-wrapped fuel. The 47.8% GIH and D grade confirm the drawback is real; sideboard filler you play only if desperate for removal.
Veteran Survivor: Strong one-drop for GW Survival that flips into a hexproof 5/4 — note the 60% opening-hand WR versus 53.4% drawn, telling you it's best curved out T1 so it survives to attack and grow. Doubles as graveyard hate (exile is at a premium here). Provisional-feeling C grade underrates it; it's a real early playable in green decks.
The Wandering Rescuer: First-pick bomb, no debate. 1.4 ALSA, 58.8% GIH, +6.1 IWD — flash convoke means you flash a 3/4 double striker in as a blocker-blowout or a lethal alpha-strike enabler, and it hands your board hexproof. The A- grade if anything undersells a card that ends games on the swing turn. Take it over almost anything.
Abhorrent Oculus: Mythic payoff that reads worse than it plays: a 5/5 flyer for 2U that manifests dread every opponent's upkeep, snowballing bodies and yard fuel. The six-card graveyard exile cost means it wants a self-mill/manifest shell (UG, UB) but 59.7% GIH at 1.5 ALSA shows it delivers even as a splashy first-picker. Ironically feeds Delirium opponents nothing since it exiles.
Bottomless Pool // Locker Room: Premium blue common-quality uncommon and a P1-P2 in any blue deck. The {U} bounce half is flexible tempo/removal-adjacent, the Locker Room half is a repeatable card-draw engine, and it's an enchantment for Eerie. Top-of-format 57.7% GIH, +4.9 IWD and 90% play rate — the best kind of low-opportunity-cost flexibility.
Central Elevator // Promising Stairs: Trap outside dedicated UR Rooms, and even there it's a build-around win-con, not a card that wins games on rate. The 52.2% GIH comes entirely from the handful of decks stacking Rooms; the 47.5% OH and D grade show it's dead weight in a normal pile. Only take late as a payoff if you're already deep into the inconsistent Rooms lane.
Clammy Prowler: Filler bordering on sideboard — the 7.4 ALSA and 20.9% play rate tell the story. A 2/5 wall that only pays off by attacking is fighting itself; the unblockable rider needs a board you rarely have when you're the one stuck on defense. 51% GIH is last-cards-in-the-deck territory.
Creeping Peeper: Narrow WU eerie enabler. A 2/1 whose mana only casts enchantments/unlocks doors is a build-around ramp piece, not a generic playable — the 51.6% and 50% play rate say it's replacement-level outside a dedicated enchantment shell. Take it late when you're committed to Azorius/Dimir eerie.
Cursed Windbreaker: Role-player, best in UG manifest-dread. It manifests, dresses the 2/2 with flying, and doubles as evasion later, but the 57.3% GIH and C grade flag it as a value piece, not removal-tier — the equipment is only good when you have creatures to move it onto. Fine mid-pick in a synergy deck, cuttable elsewhere.
Daggermaw Megalodon: Filler top-end with a floor. The 5/7 vigilance body is a fine mana sink and islandcycling {2} means it's never a dead card, but the D+ grade and flat numbers say it's a late-pick roleplayer, not a payoff. Runs in any blue deck that wants a curve-topper; nothing to prioritize.
Don't Make a Sound: Situational role-player, not a maindeck lock. Force Spike-plus-surveil is real tempo in UB/UW control but dead when they have mana up; the 34% play rate shows most decks cut it. The 55.1% GIH is the reward from disciplined tempo/eerie seats holding it for a key turn — not a card you draft early.
Duskmourn's Domination: Playable pseudo-removal for blue control, not a slam. Six mana for -3/-0 and ability-strip neuters a blocker or attacker without exiling — Ethan's "nerfed In Bolas's Clutches is still fine" won out over Ben's zero. The 55% GIH inflates because control decks that want it play it well; low OH (51.4%) confirms it's a mid-game pickup, not an early one.
Enduring Curiosity: Bomb — take it P1P1. 60.6% GIH, +7.6 IWD and an ALSA of 1.7 all agree: a 4/3 flash that draws on any combat damage and reanimates itself as an enchantment is a card-advantage engine that's miserable to answer. The B+ grade undersold it; trust the live numbers. Slam it in any blue deck.
Enter the Enigma: Filler cantrip at best — 9.3% play rate and a D+ grade are the honest signal, and the 50.6% GIH is just the small pool of tempo/evasion decks that ran it. Unblockable-plus-draw does nothing to the board in a grindy format. Leave it in the sideboard unless you have a specific reach or Eerie/ninjutsu payoff to enable.
Entity Tracker: Premium blue rare and the engine anchor for UB/WU Eerie. Flash 2/3 that draws on every enchantment or unlocked Room — 61.7% GIH and a monster +9.3 IWD confirm it snowballs card advantage in any enchantment-leaning deck. Even in a light-enchantment blue pile it's a fine flash body. High pick; the Eerie decks make it broken.
Erratic Apparition: Replacement-level filler flyer. A 1/3 evasive body that only grows in a dedicated Eerie deck (WU/UB), and outside it the +1/+1 rarely matters. 52.9% GIH and 43% play rate with a C- grade say it's a late-table role-player for enchantment decks, not a maindeck lock.
Fear of Failed Tests: Trap despite the fat toughness. A 2/7 that only draws on connect has no evasion, so in this midrange format it just stares at the board — 51% GIH, 28.8% play rate and a D grade all agree. It blocks forever but doesn't advance your game; sideboard/late filler at best.
Fear of Falling: The set's signature trap — a 3UU 4/4 flyer previewed as premium that both LoL hosts moved way down on. It dies to Scorching Dragonfire or Nowhere to Run for a fraction of its cost with no ETB to show for it, so the 55.5% GIH overstates it. The attack trigger is nice tempo but you rarely untap to use it; a middling role-player, not the early pick the flying stat suggests.
Fear of Impostors: A flash 3/2 stapled to a Cancel — fine tempo role-player in blue tempo/eerie, but the counter hands your opponent a manifest dread, feeding their yard and body, so it's softer than a clean counter. 53.9% GIH is playable-not-exciting; take it as a curve filler, not a priority.
Fear of Isolation: Premium blue uncommon — the numbers are real. 59.6% GIH and +5.3 IWD off a 1U 2/3 flyer that re-buys your own ETB or, better, self-bounces an enchantment to re-trigger eerie. Elite in WU/UB and just a good evasive body anywhere; grade C+ badly underrates it. Snap pick.
Floodpits Drowner: Premium blue tempo pick, take it early. Flash + vigilance means it ambushes, and the ETB tap-and-stun buys tempo while the two-mana ability tucks a stunned threat into the library — real exile-adjacent removal in a graveyard format that prizes tucking. 59.1% GIH understates it; the B- is low, this is closer to a B/B+ interactive two-drop.
Get Out: Flexible blue role-player, better than the C grade. Two-mana instant counter for creature/enchantment spells plus a bounce mode to reset your own ETBs or dodge removal — the +2.1 IWD shows real games-in-hand value. Solid in UG/UB tempo where you're already holding up mana; a mid-pick, not a first-pick.
Ghostly Keybearer: Fine evasive body, marginal upside. A 3U 3/3 flyer is a playable clock; the Room-unlock rider is nearly irrelevant outside a dedicated UR/UW Rooms build. 52.9% GIH is just what a mediocre four-mana flyer earns. Roster it in blue decks, don't reach.
Glimmerburst: Premium blue common — the closest thing to raw card advantage in the color. Draw two plus a Glimmer body for four mana is efficient, and the +3.5 IWD with 57.6% GIH proves it plays great anywhere, doubling as Eerie fuel in WU/UB. Take it early; blue's weak commons make this a priority.
Leyline of Transformation: Unplayable in Limited. Null WR, F grade and a 0.4% play rate — a tribal type-changer does nothing when your creatures don't share a payoff. This is a Constructed card. Never maindeck; it's not even a sideboard consideration here.
Marina Vendrell's Grimoire: Trap in Limited — six mana, no board impact, and the life-gain/loss-into-draw/discard engine is a coin-flip that can outright lose you the game with an empty hand. F grade and 0.9% play rate confirm nobody wants it. Provisional read given null WR, but this is a build-around that Limited can't support; sideboard.
Meat Locker // Drowned Diner: Strong blue common — take it highly, as Numot flags. The front door is a two-mana double-stun (near-Frost-Titan tempo), the back a three-card dig; the gap between 51.1% OH and 58.2% GD shows it's a mid-game value/tempo card, not an opener. 83% play rate and 4.5 ALSA make it a reliable UR/UB/WU pickup.
The Mindskinner: A UUU 10/1 unblockable that mills instead of damaging — a mill-kill clock, not beatdown, and it dies to any ping. 56% GIH is inflated by the games where it goes unanswered and closes fast; the C- grade and triple-blue cost temper it. Fine finisher in a controlling UB/UR mill build, but fragile and archetype-narrow.
Mirror Room // Fractured Realm: Bomb-adjacent mythic but build-dependent, so grade it as a strong playable rather than a slam. The clone half is fine value alone; Fractured Realm doubling all your triggers is the ceiling in an Eerie/ETB deck. 55.5% GIH with a big OH-to-GD gap (51%→58.2%) shows it wants to be drawn into a developed board — take it, but it's not a mono-power P1.
Overlord of the Floodpits: Bomb, slam it P1P1. Impending 4 lets you deploy it turn three, and even before it's a creature every attack-or-enter draws two and loots, fueling your yard for Delirium/Manifest Dread. The 63% GIH, +10.7 IWD, and 1.5 ALSA all scream first-pick; card selection plus an evasive threat plus graveyard fuel is everything this format wants.
Paranormal Analyst: Ben's #2 blue uncommon and "broken" in UG — but read the 56.7% as a UG-manifest-dread number, not a generic one. With a stream of dread triggers it's card advantage every turn; in a pile with two enablers it's a 1/3 that does nothing. High pick when you're committed UG, near-unplayable otherwise.
Piranha Fly: Evasive filler. Enters tapped so it can't trade on turn two, but a 1U flyer chips reliably and holds an aura; 54.4% is fine floor value. Low 45% play rate means it's a late-deck body — playable in flyers/eerie blue, cuttable when your curve is full.
Scrabbling Skullcrab: Filler/sideboard, only in dedicated UB Eerie mill. A 0/3 that mills two per enchantment trigger does nothing on an empty board — the 51.8% GIH and 58% play rate say it's a marginal enabler, and milling opponents actively feeds their delirium/reanimator. D+ is fair; play it only as an eerie payoff, not a maindeck default.
Silent Hallcreeper: Premium rare — P1P1 caliber. An unblockable 1/1 for {1}{U} that snowballs into counters, card draw, or a clone every hit; 1.7 ALSA and 63% OH WR mean it's a game-winner from turn two on. The evasion sidesteps the format's ground stall entirely. Take it over almost anything.
Stalked Researcher: Solid defensive playable in UB/UW eerie. A 1U 3/3 blocker that walls anything on the ground and turns into a repeatable attacker once your enchantments/Rooms come online. 54.1% GIH with near-zero IWD says it's a floor card — great early wall, best when eerie is turned on. Reliable common.
Stay Hidden, Stay Silent: Premium blue removal-aura and Ben's #3 blue uncommon — pick it highly. Two mana to lock down any creature permanently is real removal, and the +5.1 IWD (highest here) plus 58.8% GIH shows it carries games; the late Manifest-Dread mode is pure upside. The C+ grade underrates it — trust the live number.
The Tale of Tamiyo: Provisional pass. The 47.3% GIH sits on a 2.7% play rate, so it's noise from a handful of dedicated spells decks — and DSK isn't a spellslinger format, so the chapter-IV recast payoff rarely finds enough instants/sorceries to matter. D+ grade fits; niche curiosity, not a real pick.
Tunnel Surveyor: Fine blue two-for-one common and glue for enchantment decks — a 2/2 that leaves behind a 1/1 Glimmer enchantment body, feeding Eerie and go-wide. The 55.5% GIH and B grade are earned in WU/UB, less exciting in a random blue pile. LoL rates the creature half highly for decks needing bodies; solid early-mid playable, not a bomb.
Twist Reality: Flexible role-player, not premium. The counter mode is soft (situational in a slow format) but the manifest-dread mode makes it never dead, feeding UG's yard and board. 55.5% GIH with a 50% play rate says it's a fine value-flex the manifest decks want most; a serviceable filler elsewhere. Mid-pack.
Unable to Scream: Underrated common removal — for a single U it neuters any creature into a 0/2 with no abilities and locks face-down manifests from flipping. Ethan zeroed it at preview and was flat wrong; it settled as real Swords-at-sorcery-speed removal, best in UB/WU Eerie where the game goes long. 57.1% GIH and 90% play confirm; take it as a maindeck answer.
Underwater Tunnel // Slimy Aquarium: Solid flexible blue common. Cheap surveil for one to fuel the yard early, or a manifest-dread-plus-counter body later — both halves are enchantments feeding Eerie and Manifest Dread in UG/UB. 54.8% GIH and 77% play rate for a one-drop-optional card is excellent value; a reliable early-to-mid pick.
Unnerving Grasp: Premium blue tempo, take it early and it's a legitimate P1P1 that keeps you open. Bounce a blocker or key permanent AND manifest dread to build a body plus feed the yard — the +6.9 IWD and 60.8% GIH reflect that two-for-one flexibility. The engine of UG Simic Manifest Dread but good in any blue deck; Ben has first-picked it over committing to white.
Unwilling Vessel: Middling eerie role-player. A 2/3 vigilance that banks possession counters and cashes out as a flying token when it dies is fine value in WU/UB, but the 53.4% GIH and flat +0.5 IWD say it rarely swings a game. Playable body that fills a slot; don't prioritize it over your enablers or removal.
Vanish from Sight: Underrated tempo answer — take it as pseudo-removal. Tucking to top OR bottom means it doesn't feed the opponent's yard (premium in a delirium/reanimator format) and it hits anything nonland; the surveil fuels your own graveyard. 56.8% is quietly strong for a common. Better than its C+ suggests.
Appendage Amalgam: Filler common, last-picks-to-cut range. Flash 3/2 that surveils on attack is playable in a graveyard deck but the 51.5% GIH, 6.5 ALSA and 43.7% play rate mark it as replacement-level — you run it when short on bodies. C grade is accurate; graveyard fuel is a minor upside, evasion-free ground body is the reality.
Balemurk Leech: Filler eerie payoff — sideboard-to-fringe playable. A vanilla 2/2 whose 1-life drain only matters in a dedicated UB/WU enchantment build, and even there the drip is small. Sub-51% GIH and 38% play rate confirm it's replacement-level; only run it if your Eerie count is genuinely high.
Cackling Slasher: Sideboard filler. A 3B 3/3 deathtouch that's sometimes a 4/4 reads okay, but 46.5% GIH, 7.7% play and D grade are damning — four-mana deathtouch with no evasion or ETB is exactly what this slow midrange format doesn't want. Leave it in the box unless desperate.
Come Back Wrong: Premium black removal — take it P1-P2. Three mana to unconditionally destroy any creature is already excellent, and the temporary steal often swings a race or eats a second body via sacrifice. +5.4 IWD and 87% play confirm it's a slam; note it does feed the yard, a minor cost in this reanimator-heavy format. B+ grade is right.
Commune with Evil: Solid BG playable, better than its C grade. 56.8% GIH with a +5.3 IWD: digging four deep at instant... sorcery speed while dumping three cards to the yard is exactly what Golgari Delirium wants, and the 3 life smooths the aggressive draws. Card selection plus graveyard fuel plus lifegain — a clean mid-pick in any black graveyard deck.
Cracked Skull: Sleeper that only turns on in dedicated black shells — Ben's four versus Ethan's zero splits into a mid verdict, resolved by the 18% play rate: it's a role-player, not a maindeck staple. The hand peek plus damage-triggered kill is genuine removal-adjacent value in BR sacrifice and UB, feeding enchantment/Eerie counts. Speculative pick; great when your deck actually wants it.
Cynical Loner: Role-player two-drop for GW/BG. A 3/1 that's evasive versus Glimmers and self-mills a card on Survival — useful early beatdown that also fuels Delirium/reanimator. 54.8% GIH and 65% play rate mark it as a solid-but-unexciting body; the tutor-to-yard is real Delirium/BW value. Playable, not a priority.
Dashing Bloodsucker: Solid Eerie role-player, not a bomb. A 2/5 wall for 3B that punches for 4 with lifelink when your enchantments trigger — great blocker floor, real damage ceiling in UB/WR/WU Eerie. The B grade overshoots the 52.6% GIH; outside an enchantment-dense deck the 50% play rate shows it's a synergy card, so value it as a good complement, not an early pick.
Defiled Crypt // Cadaver Lab: Strong BG/BW engine uncommon, but its numbers come from graveyard decks. Cadaver Lab is a clean recursion half; Defiled Crypt turns any leave-the-yard into a 2/2 token stream — great with reanimation and Delirium payoffs. The OH 50% vs GD 56% split says it does little in your opener and everything once the yard is stocked; a Golgari/Orzhov mainstay.
Demonic Counsel: Sideboard/build-around outside a demon-heavy or reliably-Delirium deck. The 51.4% GIH and abysmal 9.3% play rate tell the story — a two-mana tutor that fetches nothing without a Demon or four card types is a nonbet in most pools. Only playable in BG Golgari once Delirium is online turning it into 'search for anything,' and even then it's a luxury.
Derelict Attic // Widow's Walk: Niche card-advantage room — the draw-two side is real fuel and the other door pushes lone attackers with deathtouch, but the 6.5 ALSA and 36.7% play rate mark it as a late-pick luxury, not a staple. 53.7% GIH is respectable in a grindy black deck that wants gas; a fine 20th-card in BG/BW.
Doomsday Excruciator: Trap — do not play. BBBBBB is nearly uncastable in two colors, and even resolved the library-exile is symmetric while handing every opponent a fixed six-card 'yard' to plan around. 44.2% GIH and 18% play rate confirm the F; it's a bomb only on paper.
Enduring Tenacity: Trap-adjacent; overrated build-around, take late. The lifegain-drain plus recursion reads powerful but a 4/3 for {2}{B}{B} that only pops off with a lifegain package posts a weak 47.2% OH_WR and 51.3% GIH — it wants a deck you rarely have. C- is right; the recursion keeps it a body, but don't pick it early expecting a bomb.
Fanatic of the Harrowing: Sneaky-good enabler, better than its 37% play rate. A rummage-on-a-body that loots you toward delirium/reanimator while stripping the opponent's hand — the +3.5 IWD shows it earns its slot in BG/BW yard decks. In a random pile it's a 2/2 for 4; know which deck you're in before valuing it.
Fear of Lost Teeth: Underrated common — Ben's #2 sleeper, and I agree. A B 1/1 that's an enchantment creature (two yard types in one card) and pings on death makes it perfect BG Delirium/BR Sac glue: fuels delirium, trades up, and every sac outlet loves it. 54.4% GIH undersells the synergy value; take it a touch early for those decks.
Fear of the Dark: Filler beater, borderline maindeck. A 5/5 for five with conditional evasion reads fine but the 50.9% GIH, 7.1 ALSA and 27% play rate expose it — no immediate impact, dies to Nowhere to Run/Dragonfire, and the menace/deathtouch rider is easily played around. Playable only in grindy black decks short on bodies.
Final Vengeance: Premium common removal — one of black's honest, and here exile-quality, kill spells. The sac cost is a feature: pitch a spent enchantment to also enable your own delirium, as Numot notes Kenji did at a high pick rate. 56.8% GIH understates it since removal wins by existing, not by being drawn. Take it early.
Funeral Room // Awakening Hall: Premium first-pick for any black deck, sacrifice or reanimator — the 2.2 ALSA and A- grade are legit. The cheap front half drains on every death (engine in BR sac), and the back half is a mass reanimation finisher for BW/BG. Note OH 49.9% vs drawn 58.9%: it wants a stocked yard, so it snowballs the longer the game goes.
Give In to Violence: Sideboard/filler trick — the 8.0 ALSA and 10% play rate say it all; drafters correctly leave it in the pack. +2/+2 lifelink is a below-rate combat trick in a format that punishes tricks, and its 50.3% GIH is a bottom-tier playable. Only maindeck if desperate for a lifegain race card.
Grievous Wound: Trap. A five-mana aura that does nothing on cast and only matters if you're already dealing damage — win-more in a format that punishes aggro. 43.4% GIH, negative IWD, and 10% play rate are damning; D grade is right. Never maindeck.
Innocuous Rat: Ben's sleeper is right — a quiet BG/BW staple. A 1/1 for two that on death manifests dread: a creature type in the yard for Delirium AND a 2/2 replacement, all while chump-trading. 55.7% GIH and +2.6 IWD for a common two-drop is real value; take it earlier than its stat line looks in any black graveyard deck.
Killer's Mask: Role-player, mid-pick. The value is front-loaded: it manifest-dreads a 2/2 on entry (a body plus yard fuel) and slaps menace on it, so you're paying 3 for a 2/2 with menace and a card in the yard. The flat +0.3 IWD and 32% play rate show it doesn't move games, but it's fine curve-filler for BG/UG Manifest Dread decks.
Let's Play a Game: Late-pick delirium payoff — both hosts gave it a zero as something you don't actively enable, and the 56.1% GIH is a pure BG-delirium-on number (5.5 ALSA, 45.7% play). With four types it's a flexible modal blowout; without, it's a clunky 3B do-little. Wheel it as a value card only when you're deep in Golgari.
Leyline of the Void: Sideboard-only hate, and even then situational. Exiling the opponent's graveyard hoses BG delirium and BW/UB reanimator, but it does nothing to the board and 1.1% play means almost no one mained it. No live data; provisional read — a targeted answer to bring in versus yard decks, never a maindeck card.
Live or Die: Solid two-mode playable, better in BW/BG reanimator. At {3}{B}{B} it's either a Raise Dead-to-battlefield or a hard Murder — flexibility that scales with your graveyard. 55.2% GIH and +4.5 IWD are good; note the destroy mode feeds their yard, but reanimating your own bomb is the reason to prioritize it. C+ is a touch low for a flexible instant.
Meathook Massacre II: Trap mythic in Limited — the 44.5% OH WR is the tell. Symmetric X-sac board wipe that's clunky and expensive, and the recursion clause fights against your own tempo. It underperforms because it's slow and awkward on curve; only shines in grindy black control. Late pick, not the slam a mythic looks like.
Miasma Demon: Premium uncommon — both LoL hosts' #1 black uncommon, and the 53.4% GIH badly understates it. A 5/4 flyer that turns your dead reanimator fatties into a multi-target -2/-2 sweep is a BW/BG win condition and a mid-game stabilizer against anything. This is a synergy card whose true value hides in the built deck; the B+ grade is the honest read, take it over most commons.
Murder: Honest premium removal — Numot's "take it over almost all on-color two-drops" is the read. Unconditional instant-speed kill; the 55.2% GIH understates it because removal wins by existing, not by being drawn (see the +3.9 IWD). The double-black feeds the yard, a small cost here. Take it early in any black deck.
Nowhere to Run: Premium removal, a top-3 black uncommon (LoL). Two-mana flash −3/−3 that also strips hexproof/ward and pings eerie is format-defining interaction — the 57.9% GIH with a 2.7 ALSA undersells it because efficient removal wins games it isn't drawn in. Slam it; it anchors UB Eerie but goes in any black deck.
Osseous Sticktwister: High pick in Golgari Delirium — a 2/2 lifelink that, once you hit four types, forces opponents to sacrifice/discard or eat repeated damage every end step. The 56.8% GIH and 88.5% play rate reflect a build that reliably turns on Delirium; it also feeds it (artifact type). Weaker without the yard, but BG/BR/RG hit it easily. Strong early-mid.
Overlord of the Balemurk: Slam bomb, top of any pick. Impending for {1}{B} makes it a two-mana value engine that mills four and returns a creature/planeswalker on ETB and every attack — 62.1% GIH, +10.4 IWD, 1.5 ALSA. It fuels BG Delirium and BW reanimator while grinding card advantage, then becomes a 5/5. Take over nearly everything.
Popular Egotist: Serviceable BR sacrifice engine payoff. A 3/2 for 2B that turns your dying creatures/enchantments into drain and dodges removal via indestructible-and-tap. 54.6% GIH with a modest play rate says it needs the Rakdos sac shell (Disturbing Mirth, fodder) to shine — a good role-player there, mediocre filler elsewhere.
Resurrected Cultist: Late-table Delirium-only playable. A 4/1 for three that trades then recurs itself with a finality counter — but the {2}{B}{B} delirium activation is a real ask, and the negative IWD plus 32.8% play rate show it whiffs outside a stocked BG yard. Fine 15th-16th card in Golgari, cuttable elsewhere.
Spectral Snatcher: Serviceable common top-end with a built-in mana sink — the swampcycling lets it never be a dead card, which is why 53% of black decks run it. A 6/5 with discard-ward for six is honest beef that blocks and attacks through removal, but it does nothing the turn it lands. Playable role-player, not a card to prioritize; take it mid-to-late as a curve-topper.
Sporogenic Infection: Underrated removal for two mana — an edict on entry PLUS it turns the enchanted creature into something any point of damage kills, so it's frequently a two-for-one. Being an enchantment adds eerie value. The 56% GIH and 3.9 ALSA undersell it slightly; treat it as a solid black removal pick, better than the C+ grade suggests.
Unholy Annex // Ritual Chamber: Bomb — first-pick it. 64.9% GIH and a monstrous +14.5 IWD off a card that draws you a card every turn and, once you unlock the back, hands you a 6/6 flyer that turns the drain lethal. A- is correct; it's among the best black rares in the set and single-handedly wins games.
Unstoppable Slasher: Bomb-tier rare, take it early. Deathtouch that halves life on connect and reanimates itself once means it trades up forever and threatens absurd clocks — a two-mana card that dominates the mid-game. 61.7% GIH, 1.5 ALSA and +10.1 IWD are premium; B+ undersells a repeatable evasive-damage engine that only dies for good under counters or exile.
Valgavoth, Terror Eater: Format-warping bomb, but note the ceiling-vs-floor gap. A 9/9 flying lifelinker with sacrifice-ward that swings any game it survives, plus the exile-and-recur engine is backbreaking. The 54.9% GIH is deflated by games where you never untap with it — but 2.0 ALSA and B+ grade say take it P1 and build to protect it.
Valgavoth's Faithful: Reanimator role-player for BW/BG. A B 1/1 that sacs to return a creature from your yard is a cheap, resilient engine piece — you play it turn one and cash it late for your best fatty. 54.1% GIH with the split (56.1% drawn) shows it wants a stocked graveyard to shine; solid but archetype-dependent, not a first pick.
Vile Mutilator: Top black uncommon and a BW/BR reanimator payoff — both hosts' #2. The pay-as-you-go sacrifice cost plus a 6/5 flyer that strips an enchantment AND a creature is a two-for-one that ends grindy games; 55.2% GIH is deflated by clunky-hand games. Ben's caveat holds — you want a slow enough deck to cast it, which this format usually is.
Winter's Intervention: Solid removal role-player — Ben's "goes in any black deck." Two damage plus two life at instant speed is cheap early interaction and a fine racing tool, though it whiffs on the format's 4-toughness bodies. C+ and 55.1% GIH place it right: a dependable playable you're happy to run, not a card you prioritize over the premium exile spells.
Withering Torment: Honest, premium black removal — three mana instant, kills any creature OR enchantment (relevant vs Rooms/glimmers), for just two life. The 54.1% GIH sits below flashier synergy cards but removal is underrated by GIH; 87% play rate and 3.1 ALSA say pros take it early. Minor downside that it feeds the yard. First-few-picks in any black deck.
Bedhead Beastie: Bottom of the pool — the D grade and 51% GIH agree, and the negative IWD (-1.5) confirms it makes decks worse when drawn. A six-mana 5/6 menace with no immediate board impact is exactly the overrated-fatty trap; mountaincycling for {2} salvages it as a mana-smoothing 23rd card. Last pick / cut candidate.
Betrayer's Bargain: Premium removal that exiles — 5 damage to any creature, and if it dies it's exiled, denying Delirium/reanimator fuel, which the doctrine prizes. The sac-or-pay-2 cost is real but flexible, and 57.9% GIH at 3.4 ALSA with 90% play understates its true value since exile removal is systematically underrated. High pick, especially in BR/RG where sac fodder is free.
Boilerbilges Ripper: Niche BR sacrifice payoff, not a general playable. A 4/4 that turns a spare creature/enchantment into 2 reach damage is a real removal-plus-body in Rakdos sac, which is why both hosts flagged it — but the 19.8% play rate and neutral IWD say it's dead weight without sac fodder. Speculative early, a fine role-player once you're in the archetype.
Chainsaw: Premium red equipment, take it top-of-pack. The ETB alone is Scorching-adjacent removal (3 damage to a creature for two mana), and the rev counters snowball it into a game-ending buff in a format full of dying creatures. The 60.2% GIH, +6.5 IWD, and 92% play rate confirm removal-plus-threat on one card; grade it above the B+.
Charred Foyer // Warped Space: A trap despite the mythic stamp — the -1.2 IWD and sub-50% GIH are damning. It's an impulse-draw engine that never touches the board in a midrange format that punishes durdling; the cost-reduction side is win-more. Don't let rarity fool you into an early pick; it's a build-around that mostly doesn't pay off.
Clockwork Percussionist: Excellent delirium glue and a fine aggressive one-drop. Haste chips early, and dying adds the coveted artifact type to your yard plus a free card — exactly what BG/RG delirium needs. 57.1% GIH with 81% play is a great common; take it well before its ALSA (5.2) in a graveyard deck.
Cursed Recording: Sideboard/trap outside a dedicated spells deck. The copy engine is powerful but the 20-damage clock and the fact you need a spell-dense build make it a build-around that misfires — 50.2% GIH, negative IWD and a 20% play rate say most drafters correctly cut it. C+ is generous; only UR spells slinger with real payoffs wants this.
Diversion Specialist: Solid BR/sacrifice role-player. A 4/3 menace for 4 is a real clock, and the sac-for-card-advantage outlet turns spare tokens/enchantments into gas — natural fit for Rakdos sac. The negative IWD says it's a curve-filler, not a bomb; a fine mid-pick that gets better with fodder to feed it.
Enduring Courage: Strong aggressive rare for RW/RG. A 3/3 that hands every follow-up creature +2/+0 and haste closes games fast, and the death-recursion makes it stick as an enchantment. 56.4% GIH plus 90% play is a reliable A-minus-of-live-value; the B+ grade is fair. High pick in any red beatdown seat.
Fear of Being Hunted: Overrated aggressive two-drop — fade it. Both LoL hosts crashed off this: the double-red pip is punishing, a 4/2 haste that must-be-blocked usually just trades with a two-drop, and the Slayer combo rarely sticks. The 57% GIH comes from RW/RG aggro shells that don't define the format; a fine early creature there, not a priority.
Fear of Burning Alive: Strong finisher, Ethan's #2 red uncommon. The 4-to-the-face ETB is guaranteed value even without delirium, and once online the noncombat-damage trigger turns it into repeatable removal. 57.7% GIH with a 3.3 ALSA is partly inflated by the RG/BR delirium shells that enable the second half — but even as a raw 4/4 that drains four, it's a high pick.
Fear of Missing Out: Excellent aggressive rare and a near-P1P1 in Delirium colors — 60% GIH, 1.9 ALSA. The ETB loot fuels the yard, and once Delirium is on, the extra combat plus untap is a repeatable clock that ends games. Great in RG/BR/BG. The B- grade underrates it; live numbers say take it over most commons regardless of your exact pair.
Glassworks // Shattered Yard: Premium red common — treat it near-removal. Front door is 4 damage to a creature at {2}{R}, clearing the format's four-toughness bodies, and it's an enchantment for Eerie plus a Room for triggers. 57.2% GIH, 3.6 ALSA, 90% play rate. First playable off the wheel in any red deck; shines in UR/BR.
Grab the Prize: The Ben-high/Ethan-low card, settled at a two — a rummage-plus-draw that's a role-player, not a staple. Best as a card-selection/reach engine in RG Delirium where the discard fuels the yard and the 2 damage adds up. 53.2% GIH but a 7.6 ALSA and 23% play rate confirm it's a niche include, not a maindeck lock outside that deck.
Hand That Feeds: Aggressive RG/BR Delirium two-drop that's better than its flat stats. A 2/2 that swings as a 4/2 menace once you hit four types is real pressure, and 70.5% play rate shows it makes decks — but the negative IWD flags it as a curve-filler you want early, not a topdeck. Solid role-player in a Delirium deck, filler outside one.
Impossible Inferno: Playable removal but overcosted at five mana — take efficient answers over it. Six damage kills anything and the Delirium card-advantage rider is real gravy in RG/BG, but the 6.8 ALSA and 40% play rate show most decks want cheaper interaction. A fine 23rd-24th card and a fringe upgrade in dedicated Delirium shells where the exile clause reliably fires.
Infernal Phantom: Grade-vs-data mismatch: the B is pre-data optimism, the 51.2% GIH and -1.1 IWD are the truth. A 2/3 that needs heavy eerie to swing big and a death-ping that's fine but small. Only a real card in a dedicated UR/eerie board; otherwise a replaceable mid-curve body. Believe the numbers over the grade.
Irreverent Gremlin: Strong RW/gremlins uncommon — Ethan's #3 red uncommon and the numbers back it (57.6% GIH, 90% play). Menace makes it hard to block and the loot smooths your draws while you flood the board with small bodies. Best aggressive red two-drop short of a bomb; prioritize in Boros.
Leyline of Resonance: Unplayable in Limited, do not pick. Copying single-target spells needs a critical mass of creature-targeting instants/sorceries you'll never assemble, and turn-zero it does nothing to the board. Null WR, 1.5% play rate and an F grade are unanimous — this is a Constructed card that's a hate-pick or land-slot filler at best.
Most Valuable Slayer: Above-average aggressive common — the 79% play rate is earned. A 2/4 that survives the premier removal and hands out +1/+0 first strike each attack, letting your team trade up and push through blockers. Best in RW/aggro but playable anywhere red attacks. Take it as a reliable, unglamorous role-player.
Norin, Swift Survivalist: Aggro one-drop for RW/RG, nothing more. A R 2/1 that can't block but dodges bad blocks (and re-plays the exiled card) is a fine turn-one beater, and the OH/GD split (56.4 opening vs 52.4 drawn) confirms it wants to come down early. 54.2% GIH is solid but it fades in slower decks — take it only when aggressive.
Overlord of the Boilerbilges: First-pick bomb, full stop. 64.3% GIH, +10.1 IWD and a 1.4 ALSA — the best card in this chunk. Impending lets you deal 4 to any target on a delay then again on every attack, so it's removal-plus-a-5/5 that snowballs. A-grade is if anything low; slam it P1P1 in any red deck.
Painter's Studio // Defaced Gallery: Flexible red uncommon that pulls its weight — 57.4% GIH at 84% play. The Painter's Studio half is real card advantage (impulse two), and Defaced Gallery gives a repeatable anthem for the beatdown turns; being a cheap enchantment adds eerie value. A comfortable early-mid pick in RG Delirium or any red aggressive deck.
Piggy Bank: Real RG Delirium uncommon, resolving Ben-high/Ethan-lower into a mid-B: a 3/2 for two that trades up and leaves a Treasure, giving you an artifact AND a permanent type for the yard plus fixing/ramp. The 57.7% GIH and 92% play rate hold across green decks. Best in Gruul/Jund stompy; solid, not a bomb, exactly as both settled.
Pyroclasm: Niche but powerful — a sideboard/archetype card, not a maindeck slam. 52.4% GIH is depressed because it's symmetric and dead in creature-light hands, but in UR Rooms (as Numot notes) and against RW/token aggro it's a one-sided wrath. B- grade is fair for the ceiling. Prioritize only if you're the controlling deck.
Ragged Playmate: Filler enablement common. A 2/2 artifact (Delirium type!) that grants unblockable to your small creatures — marginal on its own, best in RW token/gremlin aggro to push chip damage. Negative IWD and C grade say it barely moves the needle; the artifact type for Delirium is a quiet bonus in BG/RG, but that's the reason to run it, not the ability.
Rampaging Soulrager: UR Rooms build-around filler; effectively unplayable elsewhere. A 1/4 that needs two unlocked doors to become a 4/4 is a lot of setup for a format where UR Rooms is the weakest, most inconsistent lane. Sub-50% GIH, 8.1 ALSA and 19% play rate confirm it — a last-few-cards pick only in dedicated Rooms.
Razorkin Hordecaller: Solid aggressive uncommon, a strong early-mid pick for red decks. Haste 4/4 for five that immediately pressures, and the attack-trigger Gremlins snowball a board and feed RW/BR token payoffs like Arabella. The 58.8% GIH and 90% play rate mark it as a reliable beater; not a bomb, but exactly the kind of proactive body the weaker aggro lanes need.
Razorkin Needlehead: Strong aggressive two-drop — 2.6 ALSA, 56.2% GIH, and 86.9% play mean it goes in every red deck. First strike on your turn makes it a genuine attacker, and the draw-punisher pings for real damage against any deck that loots or cantrips (common here). Prioritize it in RW/BR aggro; a fine role-player everywhere else.
Ripchain Razorkin: Filler beater. A 5/3 reach body is serviceable, but the sac-a-land draw is mana-hungry and quietly shrinks your board — the 19.6% play rate and 7.7 ALSA say most drafters cut it. 52.8% is warm-body value; playable when red is thin, not a card you're happy running.
The Rollercrusher Ride: First-pick bomb in any red deck, exceptional in RG/Jund delirium. The X-damage ETB is already a sweeper-plus, and with delirium online every burn spell and ping deals double — a game-ending engine. 60.3% GIH with 93.8% play and +7.7 IWD confirm it wins even without delirium; the A is deserved, prioritize it P1.
Scorching Dragonfire: Premier red removal — first-few-picks, take multiples. Three damage at instant speed for {1}{R}, and the exile clause denies delirium/reanimator fuel, which matters a ton here. Both LoL hosts' top red common; Numot calls it format-defining in stacks. The 57.4% GIH understates a spell whose value is answering threats, not being drawn.
Screaming Nemesis: Premium mythic — take it P1P1. A 2R 3/3 haste that reflects any damage dealt to it and slaps a lifegain lock on the target is both an immediate clock and a punish against blocks/removal that shrugs off the format's speed traps. 61.8% GIH across the board with 92% play; the B grade is too low, this is a first-pick threat.
Ticket Booth // Tunnel of Hate: Solid red common with flexibility. The front half is Manifest-Dread fuel (a body plus a yard card) for three, the back half a finisher; 55.4% GIH and 61% play mark it a dependable playable, better in RG Delirium and Rooms shells. Fine mid-pick, not a priority — take removal and creatures first.
Trial of Agony: Cheap removal with a catch — one mana for 5 damage is efficient, but the opponent picks which of their two creatures dies, so you rarely snipe the exact threat. The B grade is optimistic; the 53.7% GIH and negative IWD say it's a good-not-great playable. Fine early interaction that gets awkward when they only have one target.
Turn Inside Out: Above-average red combat trick — one mana for +3/+0 that also manifest-dreads when the pumped creature dies, so it wins a fight AND refuels the yard/board. The 57% GIH and 71% play rate are strong for a trick because the Manifest Dread upside plays to the format's graveyard axes. Good in RG/UG; take it as a solid role-player.
Untimely Malfunction: Flex role-player with a low 25% play rate — the modes are situational (artifact removal, redirect, or Falter), so it's a tempo/utility card, not stock removal. 52.9% GIH and flat IWD confirm it's a swap-in, best as a Falter to push lethal or blank a bomb's targeting. Playable filler; leave it late.
Vengeful Possession: Situational tempo/finisher, best as a Threaten with loot upside. Steal-and-swing for 2R shines with a sac outlet (BR) to keep the creature or to alpha-strike for the kill. 57.2% GIH is conditional on those blowout turns; the C grade and 56% play rate mark it as a strong sideboard/role-player, not an every-deck maindeck.
Vicious Clown: RW aggro-only role-player, and a weak lane at that. The +2/+0 trigger needs a stream of small creatures entering, which is exactly the shallow Boros token plan the format punishes. The steeply negative -2.5 IWD and 47% play rate say it's a bad topdeck that only works on a developed go-wide board; low priority.
Violent Urge: Filler combat trick, mostly a sideboard/late card. One mana for +1/+0 first strike is a weak blowout, and the double-strike Delirium upside only matters in a green-adjacent deck that's already online. The -0.8 IWD and C- grade confirm it underperforms; run it only in an aggressive RG/RW deck that wants a cheap trick, and even then it's a marginal 23rd card.
Waltz of Rage: Premium red rare and a near-P1 — a lopsided board wipe that has one of your creatures fireball the rest of the board, then rewards the ensuing deaths with impulse card advantage. A- grade matches the 56.6% GIH, and that WR is suppressed by needing a creature to fire; in practice it stabilizes and refuels at once. Take it highly.
Altanak, the Thrice-Called: Premium green top-end — take it highly. The magic is flexibility: a 9/9 trample that draws when targeted (so removal is a bad trade for them), and when you're flooded or need to hit land drops, it cycles into a land from the yard for 1G. Never dead, always relevant. B+ is right; green's best kind of card.
Anthropede: Sideboard card, essentially unmaindeckable. A 3/4 reach for four whose only relevance is Room destruction — 50.2% GIH, negative IWD, 7.5 ALSA and 18.9% play rate all scream cut. D grade is right; board it in against UR/WU Rooms decks, otherwise there are better commons at every slot.
Balustrade Wurm: Premium green rare — take it early. A 5/5 trample-haste for 5 that's already elite on rate, and once delirium is on it recurs itself from the yard for {2}{G}{G} as a resilient finisher — perfect BG/RG top-end. Uncounterable, haste, and the recursion give it a huge floor and ceiling; A- is right.
Bashful Beastie: Good green common — solid in any green deck. A 4G 5/4 that manifests dread on death is real board presence that feeds the yard and refills after trading, exactly what BG/UG/RG want. 55.1% GIH is honest green-common value; nothing flashy, but you're happy to run several. Green is deep, so it wheels less than the number implies.
Break Down the Door: Flexible green playable — take it mid. The Manifest-Dread mode makes it never dead, and the artifact/enchantment exile is real answer coverage in a format where exile is at a premium (kills Rooms, glimmers, equipment). 55.9% GIH with 87% play shows it always makes the deck; solid in BG/RG, main it as a maindeckable answer.
Cathartic Parting: Situational flex — and quietly good in this format. Tucking an artifact/enchantment into the library (not the yard) is exactly the exile-adjacent answer you want against Rooms/glimmers/reanimator, and the graveyard-shuffle mode can reset delirium or fight mill decks. C+ and 54.1% GIH mark it as a maindeck-flex/sideboard card, best when the meta is enchantment-heavy.
Cautious Survivor: Filler 4/4 for GW — Ben's beaver comp versus Ethan's zero lands on 'replacement-level body': 30.5% play rate and negative IWD show the lifegain Survival trigger rarely swings games. It's an undercosted attacker that blanks if it can't attack into open mana. Playable in a creature-light green deck, but the last cards in; don't prioritize.
Coordinated Clobbering: Efficient green removal-adjacent common at uncommon — one mana to fight down a creature using one or two of yours, and the 79.7% play rate plus 3.8 ALSA show green decks value it. 55.6% GIH is solid; the catch is you need a board, so it's a mid-game pseudo-removal. Good pickup in any green deck, especially GW/RG.
Cryptid Inspector: Below-replacement filler. A 2/3 vigilance that only grows in a face-down/manifest deck (UG), and even there the payoff is slow. Negative IWD, 52.4% GIH, and D+ grade say it's a last-few-slots body for the manifest shell, cuttable otherwise.
Defiant Survivor: Strong GW Survival two-drop and an early pick in that deck — Kenji-endorsed as one of the most annoying cards to face. A 3/2 that manifests dread every turn it stays tapped snowballs card advantage and board presence. 55.3% GIH with 89% play rate; the engine that makes GW Selesnya tick, take it P2-P3 when green is open.
Enduring Vitality: Strong rare, take it early in any green deck. A 3/3 vigilance for three that turns every creature into a mana dork ramps you into the format's expensive bombs, and the recursion (comes back as an enchantment on death) means removal doesn't cleanly answer it — which also feeds Eerie triggers. The 56.5% GIH and 89% play rate confirm a consistent, resilient value engine.
Fear of Exposure: Mediocre despite the 5/4 trample body — the additional cost taps two of your permanents, so it lands with your board and mana crippled, a real tempo hole. -1.1 IWD and 52.8% GIH confirm it underdelivers. A curve-filler beater in green, not a threat you build around; take removal and enablers over it.
Flesh Burrower: Good green two-drop with real teeth. Deathtouch on a 2/2 trades up and blanks their attackers, and lending deathtouch on attack turns any creature into a removal spell in combat. 54.4% GIH with 78% play is solid; a reliable early play that stays useful late. Take over generic filler.
Frantic Strength: Combat-trick filler, replacement-level. Flash +2/+2 trample can steal a fight or push damage, but auras carry two-for-one risk and the 53.6% GIH with 22% play rate mark it as a deck-dependent late-pick. D+ is fair; pass it for creatures unless your aggressive GW/RW build needs the reach.
Grasping Longneck: Playable green common, nothing more. A 4/2 reach for 3 blocks flyers and trades, and the 2-life gain softens aggro, but the negative IWD marks it as an early-curve body that fades. It's an enchantment creature, so it nudges delirium/eerie counts. Fine filler in green decks; don't prioritize.
Greenhouse // Rickety Gazebo: Marginal — mostly sideboard/fixing. The front is any-color fixing, the back mills four and rebuys two permanents, but 24% play and C- say it's clunky for what it does; you're paying a card and mana for slow value. Only in mana-hungry or Rooms-leaning green decks. Don't maindeck by default.
Hauntwoods Shrieker: Premium green engine — pick it very early (1.5 ALSA). A 3/3 for three that Manifests on every attack is exactly what UG/BG want: repeatable yard fuel plus flip-up value, and the {1}{G} unlock reads your own manifests. 57.7% GIH with +4.0 IWD is strong for a common-feeling body; green being busted, this is a P1-P2 grab.
Hedge Shredder: Underwhelming for a rare — 53.0% GIH is filler-tier. A 5/5 that needs crewing and only mills two / ramps the odd land off the top doesn't dominate, and the ALSA 2.4 reflects rarity hype more than power. It's a fine green body that supports delirium, but treat it as a solid playable, not a first-pick bomb.
Horrid Vigor: Sideboard-leaning trick — deathtouch plus indestructible blows out a double-block or protects a key creature, but 27.7% play rate and D+ grade say it's too situational to maindeck. The 53.6% GIH is the narrow set of green decks that found spots. Keep one for the board against removal-light stompy mirrors; not an early pick.
House Cartographer: Solid green two-drop role-player. A 2/2 that Survival-digs for a land every turn it attacks/taps smooths your curve and enables splashes — the split between 56.4% OH and 53.3% GD marks it as an early-game body you want in hand, not late. 82% play rate. Fine early creature for any green deck, best in GW Survival.
Insidious Fungus: Underrated green utility uncommon — a one-drop that Ethan credits the show for surfacing. Flexible sac into artifact/enchantment removal or a card plus a ramped land, and it's rebuyable with regrowth for value loops. 56.7% GIH at 3.7 ALSA and 87% play back a solid, greedy-green playable; take it as maindeck flex that fights the format's key enchantments.
Kona, Rescue Beastie: Overrated rare — trust the D grade and 50.3% GIH over the rarity. A vanilla 4/3 that needs to survive tapped to cheat a permanent out is slow and fragile; the negative IWD and mediocre live numbers show the Survival payoff rarely fires before it trades. A playable body in GW but not a bomb; don't pick it over efficient removal.
Leyline of Mutation: Unplayable in Limited — cut it, it's a constructed novelty. Paying WUBRG for anything is a fantasy in a two-color deck, and the null WR, 0.1% play rate, and F grade are unanimous. Provisionally a hard pass; nothing about this card functions in a normal draft pool.
Manifest Dread: The format's engine common — a 2/2 body plus graveyard fuel plus card selection for two mana, and it's live in UG, BG, and reanimator alike. 56.4% GIH and 83.6% play are exactly what you'd expect from a glue-everywhere card. Not flashy, but a high-priority common in any graveyard deck; take it over most sideboard-quality creatures.
Moldering Gym // Weight Room: Flexible common — fixing now, payoff later. The front fetches a basic (smoothing splashes in UG/RG/Jund), and the back manifests a 5/5, feeding the yard while adding a threat. 54.7% and +2.2 IWD is fine value; not exciting, but its dual-mode nature earns a maindeck slot in green.
Monstrous Emergence: Solid green removal, resolve the split toward playable. Ben hates it because it doesn't exile and needs a big creature, Ethan rates it higher — the 56.4% GIH, 87% play rate and +2.4 IWD settle it as a real fight-plus-reach spell in green's beefy decks. Take it as your bread-and-butter removal; C+/B- range, not a bomb but a workhorse.
Omnivorous Flytrap: Strong BG/RG delirium rare — high pick when green. A 2/4 for 3 that, with delirium on, pumps your team every enter AND attack, doubling counters at six types for a runaway board. The 57.8% GIH comes from the built delirium deck; without a stocked yard it's a vanilla blocker. In-color, take it near the top.
Overgrown Zealot: Solid UG Manifest Dread enabler. A 1G 0/4 that walls the early game and taps for mana specifically to flip face-down cards is exactly the ramp UG wants — great defensive floor plus engine acceleration. 55.0% GIH with the OH-heavy split (56.9 opening) shows it wants to be early. B- is right; prioritize it in manifest decks.
Overlord of the Hauntwoods: Bomb with a low floor — take it early. Impending makes it a fixing/ramp enchantment first (an every-basic-type land) then a 6/5, so it's never dead even when you can't afford the 5-mana body. 56.6% GIH looks modest for a mythic because the value is board-independent, but +4.5 IWD and B+ grade confirm it; premium in any green deck.
Patchwork Beastie: Premium delirium glue — take it early in BG/RG. A one-mana 3/3 that self-mills to help hit delirium AND provides the elusive artifact card type is exactly what the yard decks are short on (LoL: "exactly what Red-Green delirium wants"). 58.0% GIH with a 60.4% OH-WR: it's good on curve and only gets better. High pick for Golgari/Gruul.
Rootwise Survivor: Solid GW/green Survival uncommon — haste means it attacks and triggers immediately, animating a land into a growing threat while dodging sorcery-speed removal on your creatures. The 54.2% GIH and 58.8% play rate are respectable; the ramp-into-beater plan gives late-game staying power the archetype wants. Mid-pick playable, better the more Survival enablers you have.
Say Its Name: Premium green common — LoL's top green common, "as good as Malevolent Rumble." Ignore the Altanak build-around; the base card mills three and returns a creature/land, dumping instant+creature/land into the yard in one shot, which is elite Delirium/reanimator fuel. 55.7% GIH understates it in BG/RG. Take early.
Slavering Branchsnapper: Solid green curve-topper with a floor. A 7/6 trample for six that forestcycles for 2 when you're flooded or need land — the flexibility is why it plays better than a vanilla fatty. 54.2% GIH and 70% play mark it a fine top-end common in any green deck; not exciting, but the cycling escape hatch earns the slot.
Spineseeker Centipede: Premium green common and a P1-P2 — 'green just gets absurd cards.' A three-mana 2/1 that fixes/ramps by fetching a land AND becomes a 3/3 vigilance with Delirium: floor and ceiling both strong, feeds any BG/RG/UG plan. 57.4% GIH, +3.4 IWD and 88% play rate make it a format-defining staple; take it highly.
Threats Around Every Corner: Elite green uncommon and a premier engine — Ben's #1 green uncommon, take it very early. It fixes and ramps off every face-down permanent while manifest-dreading on entry, so it's pure fuel for UG/BG Manifest Dread. The 58.5% GIH understates it because the C grade was pre-data; the +5.5 IWD and 86% play rate show it consistently overperforms as the 'pollen' that enables the hard synergies.
Twitching Doll: Excellent green rare and an early pick — 1.7 ALSA, +5.5 IWD, 60.5% OH WR. It ramps and fixes on turn two, is an artifact for delirium, and sacrifices into an army of reach spiders when the game goes long, so it's never a dead draw. Slam it P1-P2 in any green seat.
Tyvar, the Pummeler: Bomb — first-pick, wheel-proof. 63.4% GIH, +10.1 IWD, 1.5 ALSA: a 1GG 3/3 that protects itself with indestructible and hands your board a game-ending overrun-style pump. Snowballs any green board into lethal and dodges sorcery-speed removal. The B+ is a pre-data undersell; treat it as a top-tier green mythic.
Under the Skin: Premium UG uncommon, prioritize it. Manifest dread fuels the yard and the 2/2 body while the graveyard-return gives card advantage — Ben's #2 green uncommon that does two things Simic manifest-dread wants. 60.3% GIH, 2.8 ALSA and +6.7 IWD back the B grade upward; it's a value engine, take it over most commons in-color.
Valgavoth's Onslaught: Bomb-tier green rare — P1P1 slam. The 66.1% GIH and jaw-dropping +14.3 IWD are among the set's best: it makes an army of counter-boosted manifest bodies while flooding your yard for delirium, scaling from a fine turn-4 play to a game-ender late. Everything green wants; take it over almost anything.
Walk-In Closet // Forgotten Cellar: Trap despite the mythic slot — the F grade is close to the truth. Playing lands from yard and a one-turn 'cast from graveyard' window is a build-around that does little in a 40-card Limited deck; 20.9% play confirms most people cut it. The 50.3% GIH is a small, self-selected sample of graveyard decks forcing it. Pass for real cards.
Wary Watchdog: Fine green two-drop and Delirium glue. A 3/1 that surveils on ETB and death feeds the yard twice and pushes early damage; 55.7% GIH with 83% play is a dependable-common signal, not a bomb. Best in BG/UG where the surveil enables Delirium and Manifest payoffs — a happy pick 6-8 role-player.
Wickerfolk Thresher: Solid green beater — 55.0% GIH at a 92% play rate. A 5/4 for four already brawls above the format's removal, and once delirium is on it turns every attack into card advantage or ramp. The flat IWD says the ceiling is synergy-gated, but the floor is a big body that trades up. A dependable early-mid pick in any green deck.
Arabella, Abandoned Doll: The RW Boros aggro payoff and best reason to be in that lane — X drain equal to your power-2-or-less creatures rewards the token/gremlin swarm the archetype builds anyway. 59.4% GIH, 60.7% OH (a curve card you want early). Boros is the format's weakest lane, so value it as a signpost that's only great when you're committed to go-wide RW.
Baseball Bat: Filler equipment — the 49% OH and 38% play rate say most GW drafters correctly skip it. Auto-attach +1/+1 with an attack-trigger tapper is a slow tempo tool that dies to creature removal (two-for-one), and the {3} equip is clunky. 50.9% GIH is replacement-level. Last-few-cards; GW Survival wants better.
Beastie Beatdown: RG Delirium signpost and premium fight removal — for RG your creature deals its power (plus two counters once Delirium's on) to an opponent's creature, killing big things cheaply. 57.9% GIH with +4.0 IWD; the number is conditioned on the Gruul deck that turns Delirium on, so it's a slam in RG Delirium stompy and unplayable outside green-red. Take it as a color-pair anchor.
Broodspinner: Excellent BG signpost uncommon and a P1 in Golgari. A 2/3 reach that surveils 2 on entry (fuels the yard) and later sacs into a swarm of fliers scaling with your card types — perfect Delirium payoff. Elite 59.7% GIH and a massive +6.7 IWD; one of the best commons/uncommons for the S-tier archetype, take it early.
Disturbing Mirth: Strong in BR sacrifice/aristocrats, a synergy payoff to prioritize once you're in the archetype — resolve the Ben/Ethan split toward Ethan's higher take. The ETB draws two off a sacrifice and the death trigger manifest-dreads, and Ben's own point about exponential returns on multiples is real. The 60.1% GIH is deck-conditioned (62% play rate), so it's a build-around, not a slam in a random pile.
Drag to the Roots: Premium removal and the BG signpost — instant-speed destroy-any-nonland that costs just BG with delirium online. Both hosts at B, and the 57.2% GIH slightly underrates it since efficient removal wins by existing, not by being drawn. Only downside is it feeds the yard (destroy, not exile). Take it very high when Golgari.
Fear of Infinity: UB Dimir eerie signpost and a genuine problem — 'can't race it.' A recursive flying lifelinker that keeps coming back from the yard on every enchantment/room trigger; it doesn't block, but it grinds and swings the life total. 54% GIH is measured across all UB, undervaluing it in the dedicated eerie build where it loops. Strong.
Gremlin Tamer: Top WU Eerie signpost, take it very early when white/blue is open. A turn-two 2/2 that spawns a Gremlin on every enchantment/Room trigger snowballs fast — Ethan B+, Ben A-, and "kill it yesterday" is the read. 60% GIH plus 61.8% OH_WR confirm it's a proactive threat, not a build-around; the engine payoff that makes WU Eerie hum.
Growing Dread: Good UG manifest enabler, undersold by the C grade. Flash manifest dread that fuels the yard now and pumps everything you flip up thereafter — the +4.7 IWD shows it's a real engine piece, not filler, in Simic Manifest Dread. Outside UG it's a fine flash 2/2 with upside; in-archetype, a solid early-to-mid pick.
Inquisitive Glimmer: Strong WU Eerie enabler and a fine body. A WU 2/3 that discounts every enchantment spell AND your Room unlocks turbo-charges the eerie engine while blocking well. 57.5% GIH with 77% play is legit; B- undersells it in a dedicated WU/UB enchantment shell. High pick when you're in the archetype, mediocre outside it.
Intruding Soulrager: Niche UR Rooms payoff — near sideboard outside its lane. The 53.1% GIH, 6.8 ALSA and 33% play tell the story: sacrificing a Room for 2 reach plus a card only works if you're deep in the inconsistent Rooms shell. A 2/2 vigilance for two is a weak floor; take it only when UR Rooms is clearly open.
The Jolly Balloon Man: Good RW rare, not a bomb — 54.3% GIH, B grade. The token-copy ability generates a flying haste attacker every turn as a sorcery-speed mana sink, which is real reach in Boros aggro, but the 1/4 body and one-per-turn tempo cap the swing. Boros is the format's shallowest lane, so it's a fine build-around, not a reason to force the archetype.
Kaito, Bane of Nightmares: Bomb planeswalker — first-pick it. The +8.5 IWD and 1.9 ALSA are elite: he's a hexproof 3/4 attacker on your turn, protects himself, draws cards off the surveil, and locks down blockers with the -2. Ninjutsu gives him tempo flexibility. B+ grade underrates a card that takes over UB Eerie/tempo games by itself; splashable if needed.
Marina Vendrell: Trap five-color rare — the D- grade and 46.4% OH are correct; you effectively can't cast a WUBRG card in Limited without dedicated fixing. The +8.8 IWD is a mirage from the tiny 12% subset who forced it. Do not draft it as a build-around; it's a five-color-soup-only lottery ticket. Pass.
Midnight Mayhem: Strong RW aggro payoff and near-bomb in the token deck: three bodies plus menace/lifelink/haste is a surprise burst of ~9 lifelinked damage, a real finisher. 61.2% GIH and +5.3 IWD are excellent, but RW Boros is the format's weakest lane — value it as the reason to be in that deck, not a splashable slam. Great with Enduring Innocence and Arabella.
Nashi, Searcher in the Dark: Strong UB Eerie/Dimir rare but it wants the deck built around it. A {U}{B} 2/2 menace that mills-and-grabs legends/enchantments or grows itself — great card advantage in a value shell. The +5.1 IWD is huge but the 50% play rate and OH-over-GD split show it's a synergy engine, not a raw beater; a high pick when you're in Dimir, weaker as a splash.
Niko, Light of Hope: Bomb-adjacent WU mythic, take it early — it anchors Azorius Eerie. The two Shard tokens are enchantments that both trigger Eerie and cash into card draw, and the copy ability protects your best creature from removal while doubling ETBs. The 59.7% GIH and +7.7 IWD confirm it's a high-impact engine; a P1P1 in white/blue and a strong reason to be in that lane.
Oblivious Bookworm: The UG signpost and arguably the set's best gold uncommon — a 2/3 that draws a free extra card every turn as long as your manifest-dread engine ticks, which in Simic is essentially always. +7.0 IWD and 62.8% OH WR are elite. A slam whenever you're in or moving into UG manifest dread.
Peer Past the Veil: Build-around payoff for RG/BG delirium, not a generic playable. Discarding your hand to draw X (card types in yard) is explosive only with a stocked graveyard and an empty hand — otherwise it's a card-negative gamble (49.6% OH WR, negative IWD). 53% is the delirium-deck number; take it in Jund/Golgari, pass elsewhere.
Restricted Office // Lecture Hall: Strong WU control uncommon-effort rare, high pick when the deck is defensive. The white door is a one-sided-ish wrath against power-3+, the blue door blankets your board in hexproof — both count as enchantments for Eerie. 55% GIH is deflated by needing the right board; B grade is fair, treat it as a flexible removal/protection package in UW.
Rip, Spawn Hunter: Strong GW Survival signpost — high pick in the archetype. A 4/4 for 4 that, if it attacked, digs up to four differently-powered creatures into hand for a huge refuel, snowballing the survival plan. The 53.8% GIH is dragged down by non-GW pilots; in the deck it's built for it's an A. Take it when Selesnya is open.
Rite of the Moth: BW Reanimator engine piece — the number understates it. Return a creature with a finality counter, then flashback for a second reanimation, is two bodies from your yard and the core of the Shroudstomper/Miasma Demon plan. 54.6% GIH with +4.4 IWD and a 50.9/57.0 OH/drawn split screams late-game synergy card; C grade is a pre-data floor. Take it for BW.
Roaring Furnace // Steaming Sauna: Bomb-tier Rooms rare — the payoff that makes UR worth drafting. 60.3% GIH and +10.2 IWD: the front half is a scalable burn spell (damage = hand size), the back a hand-size-plus-draw engine that fuels the front. Even outside dedicated Rooms it's a splashable removal-plus-card-advantage package. Take it very early.
Sawblade Skinripper: Strong BR Sacrifice engine — the signpost the archetype is built on. A 3/2 menace that grows and repeatedly pings any target as you sac spent creatures/enchantments is both a value outlet and a reach finisher. 56.1% GIH with a +2.4 IWD is honest; it's noticeably better in a deck with fodder, so prioritize it once you're in Rakdos.
Shrewd Storyteller: Underwhelming GW signpost — a 3/3 that adds a lone counter on attack is slow, and the 50.7% GIH with negative IWD and 45% play rate confirm it's the weakest of the Survival gold cards. It needs a wide, snowballing board to matter and does nothing defensively. Role-player in dedicated Selesnya only; take enablers over it.
Shroudstomper: Strong BW top-end and the reanimator dream, but note the card is a 5/5 deathtouch that drains 2 / gains 2 / draws on ETB and attack. The gap between 51.8% OH (clunky WWBB cost) and 57.3% GD shows it's a payoff you want to cheat or draw into, not hardcast early. 55.3% GIH is real value; premium in BW reanimator.
Skullsnap Nuisance: Eerie role-player, not the premier Skullcap. A 1/4 flyer for UB that surveils on enchantment triggers — good blocker floor and yard fuel in UB Dimir Eerie, but the 41% play rate and 52.4% GIH show it's a synergy include that idles outside the enchantment deck. Solid complement in UB, filler elsewhere.
Smoky Lounge // Misty Salon: UR Rooms payoff, so read its numbers with the archetype caveat. The ritual half accelerates door-unlocking and the Salon half makes a scaling flier — good if you're committed to Rooms, but the 47.9% play rate and 5.6 ALSA say most decks pass it. The +5.7 IWD is inflated by dedicated Rooms builds; a role-player only in the C+ Izzet lane.
The Swarmweaver: Top-tier BG Golgari signpost — a genuine first-pick, grade it above the A. Two flyers on entry is already a fine rate, and once Delirium is online the deathtouch-flyer anthem takes over any board. The 64.7% GIH and format-leading +13.2 IWD show it wins games nearly on its own in the archetype it defines; in BG Delirium it's a slam.
Undead Sprinter: Strong BR rare — a 2/2 trample-haste for two that comes back bigger from the yard once any non-Zombie dies, so in a sacrifice deck it's recurring, hasty damage. 59% OH WR and B+ grade agree it's a real threat. Prioritize in BR sacrifice; still a fine aggressive two-drop in any red-black build.
Victor, Valgavoth's Seneschal: Synergy-taxed WB/eerie rare — good only in the dedicated deck. The escalating surveil → discard → reanimate ladder needs three enchantment/room triggers a turn to fully pay off, and the 51.2% GIH (low for a rare) shows how often it stalls. A 3/3 for 1WB with upside; solid in Orzhov eerie, mediocre as a splash. Rein in the ceiling.
Wildfire Wickerfolk: Solid RG two-drop, prioritize in delirium stompy. Haste 3/2 for {R}{G} that becomes a 4/3 trampler with delirium is aggressively costed and turns on your whole graveyard theme. 59% GIH and matching OH/GD say it performs even before delirium; B grade is right — an efficient early beater that scales, exactly what Gruul wants.
Winter, Misanthropic Guide: Trap rare — the 19% play rate and sub-49% GIH say leave it.
