Symmetric two-cards-each every upkeep hands opponents gas, and the hand-size clamp needs deep Jund delirium to matter, which rarely comes online fast enough. A three-color legend with a downside built in; nearly unplayable outside a dedicated shell. Pass.
Zimone, All-Questioning: Bomb — take it over almost anything in UG. A 1GU 1/1 that snowballs a giant Fractal every time you hit a prime land count generates an oversized threat for free in a ramp/manifest deck that naturally floods lands. 61.8% GIH and 65% OH are the real deal; A- is right. First-pick engine for Simic.
Attack-in-the-Box: Sideboard filler. The -2.1 IWD, 7.2 ALSA and 19% play are damning — a 2/4 that has to sacrifice itself to hit for 6 is a losing trade in a format that punishes aggro. Its only real pull is being a colorless artifact for Delirium, and there are cleaner sources. Rarely maindeck.
Bear Trap: Marginal filler. Three-plus mana to deal 3 at sorcery-ish speed is slow removal, and the 8.1 ALSA / 11% play rate show most drafters correctly pass it. The one redemption: it's a cheap artifact for delirium and a repeatable-ish answer. Playable as a delirium-type body with upside; otherwise a last-resort inclusion.
Conductive Machete: Fine colorless glue — four mana to manifest-dread (yard fuel + a 2/2) with the equipment auto-attaching for +2/+1, so it always does something and slots into any deck. The 55.3% GIH and 82% play rate reflect that floor. Best in UG/RG where the Manifest Dread matters; a solid mid-pick, not exciting, and the C grade is about right.
Dissection Tools: Colorless bomb — take it P1 in any deck. 98.9% play rate, 1.4 ALSA, 62.4% GIH: it manifests a body, then makes it a +2/+2 deathtouch-lifelink monster that trades up and races, and the sac-equip keeps it moving. Goes in every deck and wins games outright. The A- grade is right; treat it as a first pick.
Found Footage: Niche enabler, not a maindeck default. A cheap Clue that surveils 2 then draws — Ben's preview hype cooled, but it's genuinely underrated for BG/UB Delirium and reanimator, fueling the yard and feeding Abhorrent Oculus. 54.4% GIH but an 8.3 ALSA and 13% play rate mean you take it late for those specific decks, never highly.
Friendly Teddy: Colorless filler with a small upside — an artifact type for Delirium and a symmetric cantrip on death. But a 2/2 for two that draws your opponent a card too is weak, and the negative IWD plus 22.7% play rate confirm it's marginal. Playable as cheap Delirium glue if you're desperate for the artifact type; otherwise a sideboard body.
Ghost Vacuum: Excellent colorless role-player that pulls double duty — take it early, it goes in every deck. As a one-mana artifact it's premium graveyard hate against the format's Delirium/reanimator decks (exile removal at a premium here), and the six-mana overload turns those exiled creatures into your own flying army. The 56.6% GIH and 88% play rate confirm a flexible, always-useful pick that also nudges your own Delirium count.
Glimmerlight: The colorless "golden egg" — two mana makes a 1/1 glimmer token (an enchantment, triggering eerie) and equips for a cheap stat boost, while the equipment itself is an artifact for delirium. It slots into every deck and is a staple of WU enchantments. 56.7% GIH understates its cross-archetype flexibility; take it high regardless of colors.
Haunted Screen: Niche fixing, not a maindeck default. Five-color mana plus a delirium-relevant artifact type is real utility for greedy splash decks, and the D+ undersells a positive-IWD card. But 35% play says most drafters don't need it; take it when you're stretching to 3+ colors or feeding delirium, otherwise leave it.
Keys to the House: Filler artifact, marginal outside Rooms/fixing needs. Sac for a basic fixes a splash and it can toggle your own Rooms, but a 51.3% GIH, negative IWD and 37.8% play rate say it's usually a slow do-nothing. C- is accurate; run it only when you need the fixing or are deep into a Rooms build.
Malevolent Chandelier: Fringe/sideboard filler. A six-mana 4/4 flyer is on-rate but slow, and the graveyard-tuck ability is minor incidental delirium/reanimator hate. The 17.5% play rate and negative IWD confirm it's a last-slot colorless body, mostly relevant as a bring-in against yard decks. Don't main it unless desperate for evasion.
Marvin, Murderous Mimic: Build-around that mostly misses in Limited. A colorless 2/2 for {2} that copies your creatures' activated abilities needs a critical mass of good activated abilities you rarely assemble; 29% play and C- reflect that. The 50.4% GIH is a coin flip. Playable as a cheap artifact for delirium in a pinch, but don't prioritize.
Saw: Sideboard-adjacent role-player. Equipment is slow in this midrange format and the -0.9 IWD with 18.8% play confirms nobody wants it; +2/+0 plus a sac-to-draw only shines in a dedicated BR sacrifice shell that's already sacking permanents. It is a colorless artifact for Delirium — a minor consolation. Mostly a cut.
Abandoned Campground: Fine fixing — run it in any WU deck. Enters tapped early but untapped once someone's low, and a 55.0% GIH plus positive OH-WR say the fixing outweighs the tempo hit. Nothing exciting, but dual lands that also fuel a splash are worth a mid-late pick, especially in the enchantment-hungry Azorius shells.
Blazemire Verge: Playable BR dual land — enters untapped once you have a Swamp or Mountain, so it fixes cleanly for Rakdos without a tempo cost. The 54.6% GIH is normal fixing value; take it if you're in or splashing black-red (sac/Eerie, or Jund soup). Standard early-if-you-need-it pick, higher when you're playing three colors.
Bleeding Woods: Fine RG dual land — the 53.7% GIH and slightly negative IWD are typical of a fixing land (it doesn't win games, it smooths them). Enters untapped once someone's at 13 or less, so it's an aggro-leaning tapland. 60% play rate; play it in any RG/Jund deck for the fixing, but it's a support card, not a pick priority.
Etched Cornfield: Playable GW dual land, better in aggro. Enters untapped only when someone's at 13 or less, so it's an early-tapped land that turns on as the game develops — decent fixing for GW Survival. 52.7% GIH and 44% play mark it a fine but unremarkable mana-fixer; take it if you're base-Selesnya, not as a premium.
Floodfarm Verge: Solid WU fixing land and a fine early pick for enchantment/Eerie decks. Conditional untapped dual (needs a Plains or Island) that comes online reliably once you have basics; 55.2% GIH with near-zero opportunity cost. Not exciting, but two-color fixing is at a premium in a set that rewards splashing — take it over marginal playables in WU.
Gloomlake Verge: Fine UB fixing, take it if you're in Dimir — a role-player, not a priority. It taps for U or B once you control an Island or Swamp, so it's near-untapped dual fixing with negligible downside. The 53.9% GIH and +3.0 IWD reflect the small consistency edge fixing provides; wheel-able and only worth an early pick if your mana is stretched.
Hushwood Verge: Fixing role-player — untapped GW dual as long as you have a basic of either type, which is easy. Take it when you're Selesnya or splashing; the 44.6% play rate just reflects that it's only good in-color. Not a signal or a priority, but a clean early grab for any GW seat that wants a splash.
Lakeside Shack: Good fixing land — grab it for any UG deck. Untapped once someone's at 13 or less (routine by midgame) and fixes the format's #2 engine pair; 55.3% GIH with positive IWD is strong for a land that costs you nothing. Prioritize in Simic manifest dread; solid filler anywhere splashing green/blue.
Murky Sewer: Playable fixing land for UB, take it for the mana. Enters untapped once someone's at 13 or less and taps for U/B — useful in aggressive Dimir but often tapped in a slower control shell. 54.1% GIH and +2.2 IWD reflect free fixing value; C+ is right, grab it to enable splashes, not as a spell.
Neglected Manor: Solid fixing for WB/Orzhov — a real deck-smoother. Untapped once someone's at 13 or less, so it often comes in painlessly; it enables the BW reanimator splash and the positive IWD reflects consistency value. Not a card you're excited to draw, but exactly the fixing Orzhov wants. Mid-pick when you're in those colors.
Peculiar Lighthouse: Fine fixing for UR. A UR dual that enters untapped only when someone's at 13 or less — so effectively a tapland early — is playable mana in a two-color Izzet deck but nothing special. 53.8% GIH is just what a serviceable dual earns. Take it as fixing when your colors want it; C+ is fair.
Raucous Carnival: Fixing land, marginal include. It taps for RW and only enters untapped when someone's at 13 or less — awkward in a slow format, hence the -1.6 IWD. Play it in RW/Boros for the fixing, but that's the format's weakest lane; the 53.9% GIH is a floor, not a recommendation. Filler you run when you need the mana.
Razortrap Gorge: Solid BR fixing — the Rakdos analog of the cycle. Tapped-unless-someone's-low is a mild cost your aggressive/sacrifice decks pay happily. 53.5% GIH is right for a fixing land; grab it to smooth Rakdos or a Jund splash off a BG base. Utility pick, take it once your colors are set.
Strangled Cemetery: Good BG fixing common that usually enters untapped in an aggressive-enough game (13-or-less life clause) — relevant since Golgari Delirium is the #1 archetype and wants smooth mana. The 54.3% GIH and 63.8% play rate are solid for a common land. Prioritize it in any black-green build; it fixes the format's best color pair.
Terramorphic Expanse: Premium fixing and Delirium glue — Ben's top-10 common, and the 95% play rate confirms it. It fixes any splash AND adds the hard-to-get artifact/land yard type for Delirium in one card, plus synergizes with Sawblade Skinripper. The 55.3% GIH undersells its enabling value in BG/RG. Take it early in any yard deck.
Thornspire Verge: Solid RG fixing rare — untapped R or G as long as you have a Mountain or Forest, which is trivial in Gruul. Lands don't move GIH much (54%, slightly negative IWD by design), but the C+ grade undersells it: painless dual fixing is a high pick for RG Delirium and any red-green build. Take it over marginal playables when you're in those colors.
Valgavoth's Lair: Premium colorless fixing land — take it early in nearly any deck. Enters tapped for a chosen color with hexproof, so it's uncounterable, undestroyable mana that enables splashes for the format's engine payoffs. 94.5% play rate says almost every deck runs it; the B- grade and slightly negative IWD reflect that it's a land, not a spell, but the fixing value is real.
Hallowed Haunting: Build-around mythic for a dedicated white enchantment/Eerie deck; provisional read since it's null on grade but has live data. The 52.8% GIH and modest +1.6 IWD show it underdelivers as a game-warping payoff — seven enchantments to turn on the anthem is a high bar, and it does nothing the turn it lands. Only take it if you're deep in WU/mono-W enchantments; otherwise it's a durdle.
Soul Warden: Provisional read — null OH/GD/grade, so lean on 53.2% GIH and 51.3% play. A one-mana lifegain 1/1 is a classic reprint that does little in a midrange, engine-driven format; the incidental life rarely moves games and the body is negligible. Marginal maindeck at best, closer to sideboard tech against RW aggro.
Expropriate: No live data and 7UU makes it a pipe dream in Limited — but if you ever untap with nine mana, the extra-turn/steal vote ends the game outright. Treat it as a provisional late-pick windmill bomb for a controlling ramp deck; almost never castable, occasionally unbeatable. Don't build around it.
Phantasmal Image: Strong blue two-drop, high pick that scales with your board's best creature. Clone-any for {1}{U} copies your bomb or their best threat — the sac-when-targeted downside is minor when it's already a value ETB. 56.4% GIH with +4.9 IWD and 2.4 ALSA confirm it plays well above a vanilla two-drop; take it early, flexibility is the point.
Damnation: Elite bomb removal — first-pick, near-format-best. Unconditional four-mana wrath with a 60.3% GIH and +8.3 IWD; it stabilizes any board and rewards the format's slower, grindier decks that rebuild afterward. No live-vs-grade conflict (grade null), but the numbers scream premium. In black you take this over almost everything.
Sacrifice: Near-unplayable in Limited — read is provisional given null data. A B instant that sacrifices a creature for its mana value in black mana is a ritual with no board impact; the 6.5% play rate and total absence of WR/grade tell you almost no one runs it. It's a Constructed combo card. Skip in draft unless you're building something very specific.
Maddening Hex: Trap / near-unplayable despite the mythic tag. 47.3% GIH is the worst number in the chunk and the null OH/GD data plus -2.2 IWD reflect near-zero maindeck presence — a random d6 curse that punishes an opponent's noncreature spells does nothing to the board and often bounces off you in 1v1. Provisional read on thin data, but leave it in the sideboard.
Unholy Heat: Premium efficient removal — one mana for 1 damage, or 6 once delirium is online. In a graveyard-matters format hitting delirium is trivial, so this scales into a one-mana answer to almost anything. 57.6% GIH with a 2.4 ALSA confirms it plays like the burn spell it is; slam it in any red deck, and it's near-unbeatable value in RG/BR Delirium.
Collected Company: Powerful but archetype-dependent green mythic — flashing in two 3-or-less creatures is a huge tempo/card swing, but the 54.3% GIH (null OH, no grade) tells you it needs a creature-dense deck with real hit density to pay off. In a green aggro/go-wide or Survival build it's a first-few-picks blowout; mediocre in a top-heavy pile. Draft your curve to support it.
Noxious Revival: Provisional read — null WR (only 33.7% play, 4.1 ALSA), so lean on function. For one green-or-2-life it recurs any graveyard card to the top of a library, which is flexible but low-impact in Limited: it's a value/combo card, not a threat or removal. Best as a splashable yard-recursion piece in BG/UG; treat as a marginal, replaceable playable.
